findings.title: No double-check after acquiring the write lock, so cold-start loads repeat
findings.body: After the RLock fast path misses, the code takes the write lock but does not re-check entryPointAssetsCache. If N requests arrive while the cache is nil (or in Dev mode on every call), each one that acquires the write lock in turn re-reads the manifest from disk or re-fetches it from the CDN, even though the first call has already populated the cache. The fix is to re-read entryPointAssetsCache under the write lock and return early when it is non-nil and cfg.Env != setting.Dev.

findings.title: Write lock is held across file I/O and the CDN HTTP request
findings.body: The exclusive lock is held for the whole duration of readWebAssetsFromCDN (an HTTP GET with only the caller's ctx as a bound) and readWebAssetsFromFile. Until that finishes, every other GetWebAssets caller blocks on RLock, including ones that would otherwise have hit the fast path. A slow or hung CDN therefore stalls all requests that need the page assets. In Dev mode, every request takes the exclusive lock and serializes on disk and network reads. Consider doing the load outside the lock and publishing the result under a short write lock, or at least documenting this trade-off.
